objective: Keep the user's own root exclusions when the project config cannot be read, in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-wiring (branch release/0.3.0/feat/pi-root-wiring, head 7d8c92f).
scope: Security finding (validated): extension.ts ~768-782 runs the merged config read and the user-only read in one Effect.all and sets user only after all succeed; when the merged read fails (malformed or unknown-key project .holyagent/config.json, or a failing git call), failed() leads to closedSettings(undefined, undefined) (~730) and boundConfigs holds only the defaults, so a user's extra exclusions (for example pi.features.web pi-web-kit excluding web_search and web_fetch) are dropped for the root. Read the user-only config independently (Effect.result or equivalent) so its exclusions apply whether or not the merged read fails, and include it in the union.
When the user-only read itself fails, keep the defaults' exclusions and add a notice that the home-level config could not be read, so a silent loss of the user's exclusions is visible.
Tests: a malformed project config with a user config that sets pi-web-kit keeps web_search and web_fetch excluded and gated; a failing user-only read shows the notice.
constraints: Change only the ownership paths; no version-control writes and no edits under .git/ or .holyagent/.
Follow .claude/CLAUDE.md code rules; tests must fail without the fix; do not weaken tests.
Run bunx --no-install mise run build and bunx --no-install mise run verify before reporting.

Report in under 400 words; put long logs in a file under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/43946df6-456d-58c6-bea3-7e958fcb9495/scratchpad and give its path. Write a diff-file (dist excluded) at /home/user/holyagent-notes/wire-a-fix.diff.

notes:
- The user-only read now records its result itself, outside the group that fails fast, so a failing merged read or git call cannot interrupt it. The merged read and the state-folder read still fail together, so the state-folder command is still stopped and awaited on failure. An existing test covers that.
- The home-level notice is joined into the existing setup notice slot, which I renamed from `toolsNotice` to `setupNotice`. The slot is delivered once on the next run, and a root-tools failure and a home-config failure go out as one line. I did this because adding a third `before_agent_start` handler broke the handler list asserted in `packages/integrations/pi/tests/pi.test.ts`, which is outside my ownership.
- When the merged read fails and the user read also fails, for example a broken `config` command, the user gets both the failure notice and the home-level notice.
